events.title: 1 on 1 Tech Assistance / Asistencia tecnológica

cases.refreshed: Do you need to brush up on your computer skills? Whether you need assistance putting together a Word document, Excel spreadsheet, or PowerPoint presentation, submitting an online job application or other government document, or learning a new online tool, our experienced and dedicated tech tutor can help! Sessions are 30 minutes and appointments are highly encouraged, though drop-ins can be taken on a first-come, first-served basis if times are available. Register by calling the Rose Garden Branch Library at 408-808-3070 or in person during the library's open hours. Free. Ayuda presencial para usar dispositivos digitales. events.title: Delphian Lectures: Meet the Instruments & Meet the Dynasties

cases.refreshed: A lecture series presented by the Delphian Study Club - providing the opportunity for lifelong learning and friendship via lectures and events. The current series, "Meet the Instruments & Meet the Dynasties", will focus on the history and engineering of musical instruments and the composers who wrote for the instruments. Specific Lecture Topics: September 18, 2026 - Introductory class with series guest lecturer, Debora Rosengaus - Get ready, 'cause here we go! October 2, 2026 - Meet the Piano; October 16, 2026 - Meet the Strings; November 6, 2026 - Meet the Guitar; November 20, 2026 - Meet the Brass; December 4, 2026 - Meet the Woodwinds; January 15, 2027 - Meet the Percussion; February 5, 2027 - Meet the Conductors; February 19, 2027 - Meet the Unusual Instruments; March 5, 2027 - Meet the Bach Family; April 2, 2027 - Meet the Mozart Family; April 16, 2027 - Meet the Schumann Family; May 7, 2027 - Meet the Mendelssohn Siblings; May 21, 2027 - Meet the Strauss Family, Waltz Kings. This series will be presented by Deborah Martínez Rosengaus, a versatile mezzo-soprano who has studied opera, theater, music and dance, and has toured internationally with a variety of musical ensembles in concert halls such as Suntory Hall in Tokyo, The Center for Performing Arts in Beijing, Disney Hall with the Los Angeles Philharmonic, The Lincoln Center and Carnegie Hall. She has given recitals in Mexico and across the United States, giving voice to her research into the lesser-known art songs of great classical composers. Ms. Rosengaus holds a Master of Music degree from the Manhattan School of Music, where she studied with international opera diva Mignon Dunn, and a bachelor's degree from the University of Southern California Thornton School of Music. She is the recipient of several awards including the Schoenfeld Award from the Holt Memorial Scholarship Competition and 1st place in the Pacific Musical Society Competition. She has also performed in master classes with Karen Morrow and Luana Devol, and is a featured vocalist on several independent film soundtracks. She is known for her exciting, high-energy performances and for creating memorable and endearing characters such as the role of Principessa Louling under the baton of Bruno Riggacci in the world premiere of his one-act opera "Dodici personaggi in cerca di voce." She has received critical acclaim for her interpretation of Jo in Mark Adamo's Little Women and was nominated for a Theater Bay Area Award for the role of Ruth in Pirates of Penzance. Guests are always welcome and encouraged. Free. No registration required.

events.title: Cricut Open Lab

cases.refreshed: The Cricut Open Lab is a 45-minute learning session on select Fridays with machines available to use. First-time users can learn what the Cricut machine is and how it works. You can also watch these tutorial videos ahead of time to get a better idea of how to use the Cricut machine and Design Space. For those who already have experience using Cricut, they are welcome to register to use a machine independently to cut out their designs. We will have Cricut machines (Explore/Air and Maker), limited supplies, and several designs available for participants. Individuals or groups up to 3 people can register for the program. Registration required. This program is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Vineland Branch Library.

events.title: The GreenRoots Collective: Environmental Technology Workshops

cases.refreshed: Discover how science and engineering can be used to understand and solve real environmental challenges. In this hands-on Green Roots Collective workshop series, students will explore sustainability through interactive experiments, engineering challenges, collaborative problem-solving, and community-focused projects. Sustainability is becoming an increasingly important part of the world students are growing up in. Understanding how the environment works, and how everyday decisions, technology, and engineering can help protect it, gives young learners the tools to think critically about real-world problems and envision better solutions for the future. Rather than simply learning environmental concepts, students will put them into practice. Each workshop introduces a scientific idea, gives students the opportunity to investigate it through a hands-on activity, and challenges them to apply what they learn to a practical solution. Students will also contribute to community projects that connect their learning to meaningful action beyond the classroom. Through the program, participants will strengthen scientific reasoning, engineering design, creativity, teamwork, and problem-solving skills while developing a deeper understanding of sustainability and how STEM can be used to create positive change. Series Topics: 1. Floodproof! The Science & Engineering of El Niño - November 8; 2. Cooler Cities: Engineering Solutions to Urban Heat - November 20; 3. Clean Air Lab: The Science of Pollution & Filtration - December 13; 4. Microplastics Lab: Investigating Tiny Plastics in Our Environment - December 18. Ages: 7-12. Registration recommended!

events.title: Cnps talk #3 The birds, the bees and a magic trait: The evolution of red hummingbird flowers in California, a talk by Prof. Justen Whittall

cases.refreshed: Why are so many of California's favorite hummingbird flowers red? From California fuchsia blooming in the fall to western columbine, scarlet bugler, and Indian paintbrush, our native flora is full of brilliant red flowers that hummingbirds love. But is red simply a color that attracts hummingbirds, or does it also help flowers avoid unwanted visits from bees? Join Santa Clara University biology professor Justen Whittall to explore how hummingbirds and bees see flowers differently, including a hidden world of ultraviolet colors invisible to humans. Drawing on recent research with his students and international collaborators, he'll reveal how these hidden pigments may help explain not only why hummingbird flowers are red, but also how new plant species evolve. Speaker Biography: Justen Whittall was born in Santa Clara and earned his B.S. in Biology from Santa Clara University, an M.S. from Oregon State University studying monkeyflower conservation genetics, and a Ph. D. From UC Santa Barbara investigating the evolution of California columbines. Following postdoctoral research at UC Davis on the evolution of California's serpentine-endemic plants, including blue-eyed Mary, wallflowers, and jewelflowers, he returned to SCU in 2007 as a professor of Biology. He works closely with undergraduates to uncover the mysteries of plant ecology and evolution, with research ranging from the conservation of rare Santa Clara County plants—including jewelflowers, columbines, liveforevers, and Hoita—to the evolution of flower color and hummingbird pollination in California's native flora. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org.

events.title: TLAB presents: The Brave Fuzzy Author Talk

cases.refreshed: Ever wondered how to blend creative writing with the wonders of science? Join us for an interactive afternoon with the authors behind The Brave Fuzzy. Members of Pen & Pipette, a nonprofit publisher for children's books run entirely by high school students, will dive into the inspirations behind the book, explore how art and science collide, and dive into a fun, hands-on workshop where you can experiment with your own creative ideas. Perfect for curious minds, aspiring writers, and science lovers alike.
